transcript:
Header: 2026-10-21 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45 mins | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (CSM) - Tom (CTO), Sara (ML Eng), Jamal (Infra), Lina (Product)

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you all, we'll try to keep to 45 minutes. quick agenda: recap last weeks runs, look at the throughput numbers, talk continuous batching and concurrency targets, and confirm next steps.
00:18 Tom: yeah thanks Alex. quick FYI we ran the test you posted last week, saw some improvements but also some weird queueing spikes around the 10 minute mark, p95 jumped from 350ms to like 1.2s.
00:32 Priya: hmm ok thanks Tom, can you remind me which configuration you used, was continuous batching enabled or you used the default batching?
00:40 Tom: I think default, we tried enabling the batch window at 10ms, but maybwe the worker count wasn't adjusted, we did 4 replicas. the KV cache looked fine, but KVkache entries looked to be thrashing a bit.
00:55 Priya: gotcha, so two things: continuous batching will help when you have lots of small requests, but you need enough concurrency to fill the batches, otherwise you get higher latency due to wait windows, so it's a tradeoff. also if replicas are low, queue depth increases.
01:10 Sara: can you explain the filling thing again? like if we set batch window to 20ms won't that always add 20ms to latency?
01:18 Priya: good question. continuous batching is adaptive - it's not a hard wait, it will close a batch early if enough requests come in. the window is a max hold, so when QPS is high, batches close quickly and you get throughput wins. when QPS low, you might see added latency. that's why concurrency targets matter - we recommend a minimum concurrency so the windows rarely wait the full time.
01:37 Alex: and to add, Redwood also does prefix/KV caching so repeated prefixes shouldn't re-run the whole attention, but if your workload has varied prompts that cache hit rate is low, batching matters more.
01:47 Jamal: we saw a lot of variance when we ramped to 500 concurrent connections in the early run, queues piled up on one pod. Could that be a load balancing issue?
01:56 Marcus: could be, or sticky sessions, or misconfigured routing. Priya, maybe walk through the routing and worker assignment?
02:04 Priya: sure. our routing will distribute by token-length & seq len heuristics and also by model variant. if you pin a model variant that's heavier it can reduce overall throughput. Also horizontal autoscaling should add pods before queue saturates if the policy is based on queue depth or CPU. Looks like your policy was CPU-based?
02:20 Jamal: yup CPU 75% threshold, we used target throughput per pod from last quarter.
02:25 Priya: ok that explains it; CPU isn't always first to spike because of batching and queueing, use queue depth or average response latency as a trigger for autoscale. we usually recommend a queue-depth threshold plus a concurrency limit per pod.
02:37 Tom: what's a good concurrency target per pod for the m60-gpu you recommended? we are on GpuPool-xx (note: name transcribed weird)
02:45 Priya: for that class, with our optimized kernels and quantized model, we typically recommend starting with concurrency 48-64 per pod for 2k token average sequences; if you have shorter averages you can push higher. also adjust batch_max_tokens parameter.
02:58 Sara: earlier you mentioned queueing/backpressure, what does Redwood do when queue depth exceeds threshold? do you drop or throttle?
03:05 Alex: by default we queue and apply backpressure; for hosted customers we offer soft-failover to a cheaper model variant if latency SLOs are at risk, and for Dedicated you can configure queuing policy: reject, emergency scale, or fallback.
03:20 Lina: regarding cost, at what point does continuous batching stop saving money? if we increase concurrency to fill batches are we paying more because of more pods?
03:28 Priya: great point - sometimes higher concurrency per pod is better than more pods. the goal is to maximize GPU utilization while keeping tail latency acceptable. continuous batching increases tokens-per-second on a single GPU which lowers per-token cost -- but if you're adding too many pods to hit concurrency it can backfire. that's why the concurrency and batch size tuning are coupled.
03:45 Tom: ok so practical steps: we need a recommended concurrency matrix and a run plan.
03:50 Priya: we'll share a spreadsheet with recommended concurrency per pod by avg sequence length and target QPS; also include suggested batch windows and max tokens.
03:58 Alex: we also want you to run a 24hr soak test at your expected QPS with the suggested config so we can observe autoscaling and cache behavior overnight. that's when most queueing spikes showed up in your earlier runs.
04:10 Jamal: fine. we'll run 24hr. question on observability: can you surface per-pod queue depth and per-route latency histograms?
04:18 Marcus: yes we have per-route dashboards; you can get token-level cost and p50/p95/p99 histograms and trace IDs for slow requests. we'll share a grafana link.
04:28 Sara: security quick Q: for the Dedicated pilot we need KMS integration and audit logs, do you have a SOC2 attestation?
04:35 Alex: yes SOC 2 Type II, we also support customer-managed KMS (HSM integrations) and detailed audit logs. I'll resend the security pack link.
04:42 Lina: one more thing - when you say fallback model variant for latency, is that a lower-quality quantized model or a smaller architecture?
04:48 Priya: can be either; typically we suggest a quantized variant of the same architecture first, because it tends to have similar output quality and lower compute. fallback to smaller arch is the last resort.
04:59 Tom: any notable gotchas?
05:02 Priya: watch for prefix caching eviction if you have many unique sessions, that can reduce cache effectiveness; also monitor batch fill rates, and ensure your autoscaler is using queue depth not only CPU.
05:13 Alex: ok recap - Redwood to send benchmark sheet and config, Priya a sample continuous-batching config, Maple to run 24hr soak and report back, we'll meet again after the soak.
05:25 Tom: sounds good, thanks all.

(Notes: some transcription artifacts present; KV cache spelled various ways, model variant names garbled in places. Reference links shared in chat: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/maple-poc, Security pack: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2)
